# Executive Overview {.unnumbered}

Accurate spatial positioning is essential for environmental monitoring, ecosystem ecology, and remote sensing. In dynamic environments such as Amazonian floodplains and neotropical wetlands, centimeter-level horizontal coordinates and reliable vertical datums are required to align drone lidar, calibrate satellite altimetry, and track seasonal flood-pulse variations.

When working in remote field sites without cellular internet, real-time RTK positioning is unavailable. Field researchers must record raw satellite observations and post-process them in the office.

This manual provides an end-to-end, pedagogical walkthrough for graduate students and early-career researchers with no prior geodetic post-processing experience.

## Structure of this Manual

1. **[Foundations of GNSS Post-Processing for Field Researchers](#sec-foundations):** Explains relative (PPK) vs. absolute (PPP) positioning, the Brazilian SIRGAS2000 reference frame, the critical difference between ellipsoidal ($h$) and orthometric ($H$) heights, and antenna geometry (ARP vs. APC).
2. **[Downloading and Preparing IBGE RBMC Reference Station Data](#sec-ibge-rbmc):** Guides you through finding the nearest reference station in the Brazilian continuous network, downloading 24-hour observation and broadcast navigation files from GeoFTP, interpreting official station reports (*Relatório da Estação*), and decompressing Hatanaka files with `CRX2RNX`.
3. **[Post-Processing Kinematic (PPK) in Emlid Studio](#sec-emlid-studio-ppk):** Walkthrough of the Emlid Studio GUI on Windows, pairing raw Emlid Reach RS2 logs with RBMC base station data, configuring the 134 mm antenna offset, overriding base station coordinates, and evaluating Fix vs. Float solutions.
4. **[Preparing RINEX Observations with RTKlib: 30-Second Decimation and Formatting](#sec-rtklib-prep):** Explains why static PPP requires 30-second epoch intervals, and provides a step-by-step tutorial using the RTKCONV GUI to decimate high-rate files and format standard headers.
5. **[Submitting to IBGE PPP and Interpreting Geodetic Reports](#sec-ibge-ppp):** Details online submission to the IBGE PPP service, choosing antenna calibration models, and reading the official PDF report to extract SIRGAS2000 coordinates, formal standard deviations, and MAPGEO2015 orthometric heights.
6. **[Troubleshooting, Practical Pitfalls, and Field Checklist](#sec-troubleshooting):** Diagnoses common issues (the "Float-only" trap, canopy cycle slips, Hatanaka ingestion failures, height offset errors) and provides a field checklist for future campaigns.
